edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 20 November 2026 and 10:00 AM IST on 21 November 2026

items.caseName: Rossi Gearmotors (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Spartan Engineering Industries Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey (Judicial Member) and Prabhat Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Pending cheque bounce complaints do not bar CIRP if Section 9 admission criteria are met
items.text: In an order dated 19 November, NCLT Mumbai held that pending complaints under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act do not stop an operational creditor's Section 9 IBC petition when the admission requirements are satisfied. It rejected the pre-existing dispute plea because the debtor had not shown its grievance about the gearboxes was still live when the demand notice arrived, and the disputed goods were a small part of a supply already paid for. CIRP was started, an IRP appointed and a moratorium declared.

items.caseName: In the matter of Narendra Mithailal Agarwal
items.coram: Sushil Mahadeorao Kochey (Judicial Member) and Prabhat Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Co-borrower's independent repayment liability is not a personal guarantee
items.text: NCLT Mumbai held on 19 November that a co-borrower's repayment obligation is an independent liability. It cannot be treated as a personal guarantee just because the same person also guaranteed another entity's debt. The tribunal distinguished the NCLAT ruling in Syed Sirajis Salikin Khadri, rejected the claim that the Section 94 plea was filed to obstruct SARFAESI recovery, admitted the personal insolvency application and imposed a 180-day moratorium.

items.caseName: Dilipkumar Natvarlal Jagad, Liquidator of Naturell (India) Private Limited
items.coram: Shammi Khan (Judicial Member) and Sanjeev Sharma (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Ahmedabad declines dissolution of 'Ritebite Max Protein' maker Naturell India over EPFO dues
items.text: In an order dated 18 November, the Ahmedabad bench refused to dissolve Naturell under Sections 59(7) and 59(8) of the IBC. It was not satisfied that the company's affairs had been fully wound up, pointing to an EPFO claim of about Rs 14.51 lakh, mismatches between Form H and the liquidation accounts, and an unexplained transfer of the business to the parent company. The plea was disposed of as premature, and the liquidator may file afresh once the defects are fixed.

items.caseName: Rajendra Dallaram Choudhary v. Kiran Shah
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr V.G. Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: Going-concern sale in liquidation is not equivalent to revival under a resolution plan
items.text: NCLT Ahmedabad held on 17 November that a going-concern sale during liquidation cannot be equated with reviving the company under an approved resolution plan. It refused the buyer's request for concessions and exemptions, noting that the company had been in liquidation for over six years, the late sale lacked prior approval and no valuation showed goodwill that would justify relief. The transaction was to be treated as a slump sale, so blanket concessions were denied.

items.caseName: In the Matter of L&T Power Development Limited and Larsen & Toubro Limited
items.coram: Nilesh Sharma (Judicial Member) and Charanjeet Singh Gulati (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Mumbai dispenses with L&T shareholder and creditor meetings for merger of wholly owned subsidiary
items.text: On 19 November the tribunal waived shareholder and creditor meetings for merging L&T Power Development Limited into its parent, Larsen & Toubro. It reasoned that the scheme neither dilutes L&T's shareholding nor affects creditors' rights, since the subsidiary's shares will be cancelled without issuing new ones. L&T was instead directed to notify its shareholders and creditors individually, who may file representations within 30 days, and to notify regulators and tax authorities.

items.caseName: GRICL Rail Bridge Development Authority Company Ltd
items.coram: Chitra Hankare (Judicial Member) and Dr V.G. Venkata Chalapathy (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Ahmedabad orders winding up of IL&FS subsidiary GRICL Rail Bridge Development Company
items.text: In an order dated 4 November, the Ahmedabad bench ordered the winding up of this wholly owned subsidiary of Gujarat Road and Infrastructure Company, part of the IL&FS group. The company had stopped operating and had no revenue after its railway overbridge concession with the Gujarat government was terminated in December 2021. With shareholder approvals in place and no objection from the ROC or the Income Tax Department, the Official Liquidator attached to the Gujarat High Court was appointed Company Liquidator.

items.caseName: Vishal Chaudhary v. Bangla Foods Private Limited
items.coram: Justice Mayank Kumar Jain (Judicial Member) and A. Venu Prasad (Technical Member)
items.headline: GSTAT dismisses Department's appeal over Rs 1.36 lakh IGST demand as below Rs 20 lakh monetary limit
items.text: The Principal Bench dismissed the Department's appeal because the disputed tax of about Rs 1.36 lakh was far below the Rs 20 lakh threshold in the CBIC circular. The Department had not shown that any exception applied, such as the issue recurring in other periods. The tribunal did not decide the reverse-charge IGST question and criticised the Department for filing the appeal despite the limit.

items.caseName: Shailendra Kumar Singh v. Kamlesh Trading Company
items.coram: Ajeet Singh (Judicial Member) and Vivek Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Unaccounted stock cannot be confiscated under Section 130 without first determining tax
items.text: GSTAT Agra held on 19 November that finding unaccounted stock during an inspection does not, by itself, justify confiscation proceedings under Section 130. The proper officer must first determine the tax on those goods under Section 73 or 74. The Department's appeal was dismissed, which upheld the setting aside of a Rs 1,45,055 penalty and fine.

items.caseName: Commissioner State Tax, U.P. (Through Amit Kumar Singh) v. Tempsens Instruments India Limited
items.coram: Ajeet Singh (Judicial Member) and Vivek Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Failure to update Part B of e-way bill, without intent to evade tax, cannot attract Section 129 penalty
items.text: GSTAT Agra held on 19 November that failing to update Part B of an e-way bill does not, by itself, attract a penalty under Section 129(3) when there is no evidence of intent to evade tax. Genuine documents travelling with the goods rebutted any presumption of evasion, and Uttar Pradesh, being only a transit state, lacked penal jurisdiction. The cancellation of the penalty was upheld and the Department's appeal dismissed.

items.bench: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Kupwara (J&K)
items.caseName: Ghulam Nabi Magray v. Executive Engineer, KPDCL, Division Handwara
items.coram: Peerzada Qousar Hussain (President) and Nyla Yaseen (Member)
items.headline: Kupwara Consumer Commission quashes Rs 2.1 lakh joint-family electricity dues billed to new house
items.text: The commission quashed a Rs 2.1 lakh electricity bill after the power department shifted the complainant's dues from his jointly owned family home to his newly built house. It held that the department's failure to correct the billing details, even after a 2018 inspection and disconnection, was a deficiency in service. KPDCL was told to issue a fresh bill for the new house if it has a connection and to pay Rs 10,000 in costs, while the complainant stays liable for the old house's dues.
